summary: Approved. The reactory-azure page is the strongest form of documentation this ticket could produce: it states the module is an example-only MIT reference rather than a commercial integration, reconciles the stale registry value with evidence and an exact out-of-repo fix, and then uses the module as a ten-step build walkthrough in which every step points at a real file and line. I re-derived the load-bearing technical claims from the server checkout rather than trusting the page or the agent-authored verifier: 8 declared / 9 implemented interface methods, the getEmails omission and its TS2353/TS2339 consequence, the unimported Client/ResponseType and undeclared Graph packages, sendEmail's caught error plus the truthy Express response, getEmails' factory-before-try ordering, the commented-out storage scaffold, the empty services/workflows arrays, the MIT-vs-commercial split, and the two direct core imports — all accurate. The three verifiers run clean (azure 34/34, reactor 11/11, core 25/26) and the single core failure reproduces on origin/master 8ba69be, so it is not introduced here. The only residue is cosmetic: three loose line ranges in the reactory-google comparison, one confusing sentence about section renumbering, and the unavoidable fact that the registry still says 'commercial' until a server-side ticket changes it.
